nodes.name: Impregnation-Annealing Ru/C
nodes.procedure: 100 mg XC-72 was added into 8 mL water and treated by ultrasound for 10 min, after which 0.1 mmol RuCl₃ was added to the aqueous mixture. The mixture was kept stirring for 12 h for impregnation and evaporated at 200°C for another 16 h. The obtained black powder was annealed in 3% H₂/Ar at 800°C for 1 h.

nodes.name: Impregnation-Annealing Pt-Ru/C variants
nodes.procedure: To obtain Pt doped Ru/C (1%Pt-, 3%Pt-, 10%Pt-, 20%Pt- and 50%Pt-Ru/C), controlled amount of H₂PtCl₆ aqueous solution was added simultaneously with RuCl₃. 100 mg XC-72 was added into 8 mL water and treated by ultrasound for 10 min, after which 0.1 mmol RuCl₃ and controlled amount of H₂PtCl₆ were added to the aqueous mixture. The mixture was kept stirring for 12 h for impregnation and evaporated at 200°C for another 16 h. The obtained black powder was annealed in 3% H₂/Ar at 800°C for 1 h.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal TiO2
nodes.procedure: The mixture containing 1.5 mL 40% hydrofluoric acid and 12.5 mL tetrabutyl titanate was transferred into 25 ml Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave and maintained at 180°C for 36 h, after which the white powder was washed, dried and annealed at 300°C for 2 h to obtain TiO₂.
nodes.source_text: For the synthesis of TiO₂, the mixture containing 1.5 mL 40% hydrofluoric acid and 12.5 mL tetrabutyl titanate... annealed at 300°C for 2 h.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal CeO2
nodes.procedure: The 50 ml aqueous solution containing 12.5 g NaOH and 1.085g Ce(NO₃)₂·6H₂O was transferred into 100 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave and maintained at 100°C for 24 h. After washing using water, the powder was dried and annealed at 500°C for 2 h to obtain the CeO₂ powder.
nodes.source_text: For the synthesis of CeO₂, the 50 ml aqueous solution containing 12.5 g NaOH and 1.085g Ce(NO₃)₂·6H₂O... annealed at 500°C for 2 h.

nodes.name: Pt Impregnation on TiO2
nodes.procedure: The Pt loading on TiO₂ was achieved by mixing controlled amount of H₂PtCl₆ solution into 40 ml aqueous mixture contained 200 mg TiO₂ and getting stirred for 6 h. After centrifugation, the powder was dried and further annealed in 3% H₂/Ar at 800°C for 1 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/C shows hexagonal close-packed (hcp)-type Ru crystal structure. After incorporating Pt at low loadings, hcp-Ru structure is preserved with no diffraction peak of fcc-Pt observed until Pt reaches 10%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Based on the X-ray diffraction (XRD) results in Supplementary Fig. 2, Ru/C sample shows the hexagonal close-packed (hcp)-type Ru crystal structure. After incorporating Pt to Ru/C, the hcp-Ru structure is preserved, while no diffraction peak of face centered cubic (fcc)-Pt is observed until the Pt atomic ratio reaches 10%

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/C shows uniform distribution of Ru NPs on carbon black with grain size of ~1 nm. 3%Pt-Ru/C shows similar particle size with bright dots attributed to atomically dispersed Pt atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1b and Supplementary Fig. 3a show the HAADF-STEM images of Ru/C, which display the uniform distribution of Ru NPs on carbon black particles with the Ru NPs grain size of ~1 nm. For 3%Pt-Ru/C in Fig. 1c... the emergence of the bright dots... is attributed to the atomically dispersed Pt atoms

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-K edge XANES of Ru/C and Pt·Ru/C (1%Pt, 3%Pt, 10%Pt) shows absorption edges at higher position than metallic Ru foil, indicating high valence states of Ru. Pt incorporation causes redshift of absorption edge indicating decreased Ru valence state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1d displays the Ru-K edge X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) spectroscopy. The absorption edges of Ru/C and Pt·Ru/C (1%Pt, 3%Pt and 10%Pt-Ru/C) samples locate at obviously higher position than the metallic Ru foil... after introducing Pt, the redshift of the absorption edge together with the decreased Ru-O bond

nodes.characterization_summary: Considerable Ru-O coordination observed in Ru/C and Pt·Ru/C samples. Pt introduction decreases Ru-O bond and increases Ru-Ru/Pt bond, indicating reduced oxidation degree of Ru.
nodes.evidence_snippet: based on the coordination structures obtained from the Ru-K edge extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectra in Fig. 1e, considerable Ru-O coordination is observed in Ru/C and Pt·Ru/C samples

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Ru-K edge XANES shows Ru/C and Pt·Ru/C switch from ex-situ oxide-rich to metallic state under HOR conditions. Ru/C absorption edge blueshifts (oxidizes) with increasing anodic potential while Pt·Ru/C oxidation is suppressed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 3a... under the potential ranging from -0.05 V to +0.50 V, the Ru-K edge spectra of Ru/C and Pt·Ru/C samples show similar contour as Ru foil... the absorption edge of Ru in Ru/C obviously shifts to higher energy with increased anodic potential, while such blueshift in Pt·Ru/C system becomes less apparent

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/C shows strengthened Ru-O coordination and decreased Ru-Ru bond with increasing potential. 3%Pt-Ru/C maintains Ru-Ru coordination with Ru-O increase only at very high potentials.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 3c, d... as potential increases, the Ru-O coordination of Ru/C becomes strengthened and Ru-Ru bond is decreased, while for 3%Pt-Ru/C, the intensity increase of Ru-O bond only appears at high potentials up to 0.5 V

nodes.characterization_summary: 3%Pt-Ru/C shows Pt-Ru bond shorter than Pt-Pt in Pt/C and Pt-O_L bond due to adsorbed oxygen-containing intermediates. Coordination numbers of Pt-O_L (~3) and Pt-Ru (~6) remain stable.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Pt single atom is further verified by the operando Pt L3 edge EXAFS displayed in Fig. 3f, where the Pt-Ru bond is shorter than the Pt-Pt bond in Pt/C... Pt-O bond is also observed... the coordination structure of Pt in 3%Pt-Ru/C is quantitatively fitted with the Pt-O_L and Pt-Ru paths

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/C shows strengthened Ru-O_S (short, strongly bonded O) and decreased Ru-O_L (long, interfacial water) with increasing potential. 3%Pt-Ru/C preserves Ru-O_L coordination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 4a, b shows the operando FT-EXAFS spectra of Ru/C and 3%Pt-Ru/C... for Ru/C, as anodic potential increases... the intensity of Ru-O_S coordination is strengthened, while... Ru-O_L is decreased... for 3%Pt-Ru/C with anti-oxidation property, the Ru-O_L is preserved

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/C shows positive peak at ~3500 cm⁻¹ indicating diluted interfacial water network at anodic potentials. 3%Pt-Ru/C maintains dense hydrogen-bonded water network.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Based on the SR-FTIR spectra in Fig. 4e, f, the region of 3000-4000 cm⁻¹ is attributed to the interfacial water... For Ru/C, as anodic potential increases, a positive peak at ~3500 cm⁻¹ emerges... After introducing Pt, for 3%Pt-Ru/C... the negative peaks suggest dense hydrogen network

nodes.characterization_summary: ECSA obtained by Cu underpotential deposition-stripping method for Pt-Ru/C catalysts. ECSA-normalized exchange current densities show volcano trend with 3%Pt-Ru/C optimal.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the electrochemical surface area (ECSA) was obtained by Cu underpotential deposition (Cu_upd)-stripping method (Supplementary Fig. 9) and the corresponding ECSA normalized exchange current densities (j_0,ECSA) were calculated (Fig. 2c). As Pt loading increases, a volcano-type trend is observed
